title: Iterative discovery of potent polymeric antibiotics via multi-stage and multi-task learning against antimicrobial resistance
summary: PolyCLOVER integrated multi-stage learning, active learning and high-throughput experiments across a ~100,000-member poly(β-amino ester) space, identifying three lead nanoparticles with measured antibacterial activity and in-vivo mouse outcomes. Mouse groups were small; this does not establish human efficacy or safety.
ai_technology: Multi-stage self-supervised learning and active learning coupled to high-throughput experimentation
organization: Zhejiang University; Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Primary Nature abstract/full text reports experimental MICs of 4 and 8 μg/mL against named resistant bacteria and mouse infection models; this is one study, not three discoveries.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and exhaustive prior-art review are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Multi-stage self-supervised learning and active learning coupled to high-throughput experimentation

source_review.scope: Primary source checked for study identity, stated AI contribution, date and bounded result.
